title: PQC Transition Readiness: SQUIRL OS Position Against NISTIR 8547 Final and the Federal PQC Deadlines
description:
Technical readiness record for the SQUIRL OS prototype stating its position against the post-quantum cryptography standards and deadlines in force as of October 30, 2026. Version 1.2.

Correction carried in this version. Version 1.1 stated that key establishment had migrated to ML-KEM-1024 and described the position as at the CNSA 2.0 parameter level. Measurement does not support that. TLS group enumeration on both public hosts shows hybrid X25519MLKEM768 offered and ML-KEM-1024 not offered on either. Post-quantum key establishment is genuinely present, and it sits one parameter set below the one CNSA 2.0 names. The installed group is the content delivery network's hybrid default rather than a project selection, so attributing it to this project would have been inflation. Readers who took the ML-KEM-1024 figure from version 1.1 should treat it as superseded.

This version also replaces a plan with a measurement on signatures. ML-DSA-87 is implemented and the parameters were verified against the FIPS 204 tables: public key 2592 bytes, secret key 4896 bytes, signature 4627 bytes, roundtrip true. A category-3 signature was measured to fail against a category-5 key, which is why sign and verify dispatch on each key record's own recorded type rather than assuming a parameter set. The HMAC-SHA256 construction that previously stood in for a signature under a key type naming ML-DSA has been deleted, and surviving rows carrying it are refused with an explicit reason.

The governing standards position is unchanged from version 1.1: final NISTIR 8547 (2026-10-27) deprecates all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms after 2030 and disallows them after 2035; CNSA 2.0 requires ML-KEM-1024 and ML-DSA-87 at every classification level; SLH-DSA, while hash-based and FIPS 205 compliant, is not approved for any use in National Security Systems, and the only approved hash-based options for firmware and software validation are LMS or XMSS per SP 800-208. HashML-DSA is not permitted in CNSA 2.0.

Remaining open items are stated explicitly: ML-KEM-1024 is not obtainable at present transport settings; no LMS or XMSS implementation exists; the signature code is committed but not deployed, so running instances keep the previous parameter set until redeployment and key rotation; and one deployed signing function has no available source and remains unassessed. The companion component inventory records each of these with an evidence level.

No certification and no compliance attestation is claimed. SQUIRL OS is a prototype provided for educational and research purposes.
